messages.content: How do I find the angle of the force for a given momentum?

function.name: calculate_vector_angle
function.description: Calculate the angle of a vector based on its X and Y components. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

X_component.description: The X component of the vector. This is a float type value.

Y_component.description: The Y component of the vector. This is a float type value.

use_degrees.description: If true, the result will be in degrees. If false, the result will be in radians. Default is false.

message.reasoning: The user asks: "How do I find the angle of the force for a given momentum?" They want to find the angle of the force for a given momentum. They might be asking about physics: Force is related to change in momentum over time: F = dp/dt. But they ask "angle of the force for a given momentum". Perhaps they have a vector momentum p, and they want the angle of the force vector? But force is derivative of momentum. If momentum is known as a vector, the direction of force depends on how momentum changes. If momentum is constant, force is zero. If momentum changes, the direction of force is along the change in momentum. So maybe they want to compute the angle of a vector given its components. They mention a tool: calculate_vector_angle.
